name: System
description: CPU and memory with a one-minute trace, per-core load, commit charge, disk space, network and uptime
author: Lattice

sections.title: What it reads
items: CPU and memory as a percentage, plus a trace of the last minute for both.
One bar per logical core, so a single pegged core is visible on a 16-core machine.
Memory also shows commit — used against the limit, which includes the page file.
Free space on the system volume, network down and up per second, process count, and how long the machine has been up.
The platform samples once a second; the card only draws what it is handed.

sections.title: Reading the trace
items: The line is history, newest on the right. It fills in from the right as samples arrive, so a card you just opened shows a short line, not a flat one.
CPU is the filled line; memory is the dashed one. Both use the same 0–100% scale, so you can compare them directly.
A tall spike with a flat memory line is a burst; a slowly rising memory line is a leak.
The trace covers one minute and is kept in the card — nothing is written to disk.

sections.title: Reading the core bars
items: One bar per logical core, left to right, height is that core's load.
A whole-machine figure of 6% on a 16-core machine can mean one core at 100% or all of them idle. The bars tell the two apart.
They disappear for a tick if the core count changes — waking from sleep or a hot-plug — rather than drawing the wrong core's load.

sections.title: Why the numbers look low
items: CPU is the total across all cores — one busy core on a 16-core machine reads about 6%.
Memory is physical RAM in use, so a machine with a lot of cache can sit high and still be fine. Watch commit for the number that actually fails allocations.
Disk is the system volume only; other drives are not counted.

sections.title: It stops when you cannot see it
items: Hiding the card or minimising the window stops the sampling — a monitor nobody is looking at should not cost anything.
It picks up again on the first tick after it becomes visible, so the first reading after that is already current.

sections.title: If it shows dashes
items: The platform refused to read system metrics. The widget needs the system monitor permission.
Grant it again and the card recovers on its next tick — no restart needed.

changes: A one-minute trace of CPU and memory, so a burst and a slow climb look different.
One bar per logical core — a single pegged core no longer hides behind a low whole-machine average.
Memory gained the commit charge against its limit, and free space replaces the bare disk percentage.
Uptime and the process count join the footer; threads and handles are one hover away.
The card grew to 268×240 to fit the trace; it still works down to 220×210.
First release: CPU, memory, disk and network, sampled once a second by the platform.
Starts on the top layer so it stays readable over other windows; the inspector can pin it to the desktop instead.
